title: Shanghai Fried Noodles (Cu Chao Mian)
ingredients: 1 lb thick fresh Shanghai wheat noodles (or thick udon noodles)
8 oz pork loin, chicken thigh, or shiitake mushrooms, thinly sliced
3 cups baby bok choy or Napa cabbage, chopped
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced
2 tbsp dark soy sauce (for rich mahogany color and caramel notes)
1.5 tbsp light soy sauce & 1 tbsp oyster sauce
1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp white pepper, 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
1 tbsp Shaoxing rice wine + 1 tsp cornstarch (for velvet marinade)
2 tbsp neutral oil for high-heat wok stir-frying
instructions: Marinate sliced pork or chicken with Shaoxing wine, 1 tsp light soy sauce, and cornstarch for 10 minutes. Whisk remaining dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, white pepper, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Parboil fresh Shanghai noodles 1 minute shy of package instructions, drain, rinse under cold water to prevent sticking, and toss with 1 tsp oil.
Heat wok over high heat until smoking. Sear the pork/chicken for 2 minutes, add sliced shiitake mushrooms and bok choy stems, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, bok choy leaves, and the dark soy sauce mixture. Toss vigorously over high heat for 2–3 minutes until every noodle is glossy, smoky, and caramelized.
sourceTitle: The Woks of Life · Shanghai Fried Noodles
